indicators.note: one piece eating another means the first holds the second inside it

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A youngster drinking coffee gets complimented.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive or insincere compliments are a form of praise, a direct synonym.

definitions.meaning: a Disney film musical about an ice queen
P is Planet: his polar series was '... Planet'

explanation.surface: A musical made from the naturalist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for Planet; the series is Frozen Planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Disney animated musical shares its title with the polar half of the series name.

clue.text: Where glasses come in shades of night

definitions.text: Where glasses come in shades of night

parts.words: Where glasses come in shades of night
parts.note: shades are sunglasses; drinking glasses come out once evening falls

explanation.surface: Spectacles available in nocturnal colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shades' looks like colours; it is sunglasses, and the glasses are drinks after nightfall.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means once night has fallen, which is when the drinks are poured.

indicators.note: letters set loose are freed to fall into a new order
a bird's wings are at its sides, so the outer letters of the bird's name

explanation.surface: Releasing a heron-like bird by its wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings' takes E and T, the outside letters of egret, mixed with THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A full set in the mouth: dentures or natural gnashers come as a set.

parts.note: to rub is to chafe or annoy
the naturalist is a national icon

explanation.surface: A one-way crossing could annoy the famous naturalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Caesar crossed the river Rubicon, a step that could not be undone.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing this river was Caesar's point of no return, so it is any irreversible step.

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
an orb is a sphere, something round

explanation.surface: A sailor drinks his round at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To take in fully, as a sponge does water or a student does facts.

clue.text: Regularly jeer at bottom of fat crybaby

indicators.note: in a down entry, at the bottom puts the letters after the other piece
regularly takes every other letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Taunting someone fat as a crybaby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes E and R, the even letters of jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who weeps noisily, a sobber, is a crybaby.

definitions.meaning: used as a verb, to surpass
an open-air party, a do held outdoors

explanation.surface: A superior outdoor party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb; the second reading splits into outdoors plus a do, slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or exceed someone is to better them.

indicators.note: letters swimming about move into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Shakespeare doing lengths of the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'widths' looks like swimming lengths; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural synonym: widths are measurements from side to side.

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of the two words are staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: Two people who've been drinking are heading out of the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' is the tide, not the drinkers leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A tide that is ebbing is receding or going out; figuratively, declining.

definitions.meaning: a family member, a parent's sister
the BBC, where the naturalist made his programmes, has a fond nickname for an elderly female relative

explanation.surface: A relative living in the famous naturalist's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 18, 14, 16 spell out SIR DAVID F ATTEN BOROUGH, the naturalist turning 90 when this ran. 'Auntie Beeb' is a British nickname for the BBC.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister is a relation; the BBC's affectionate nickname is the same word.

clue.text: Group stick card to driver's sandwich

definitions.meaning: a society or association
a heavy cudgel
a black playing-card suit
a golfer's driver is one of the set used
a triple-decker sandwich

explanation.surface: A society glues a card to a golfer's sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: Five definitions; a driver is a golf implement.
explanation.definitionFit: Five senses: society, cudgel, card suit, golf implement and triple-decker sandwich.

parts.note: L and P stand for Life and Planet: the naturalist made 'Life on ...' and 'Planet ...', both named after our world

explanation.surface: A record by the naturalist and what it is on.
explanation.walkthrough: LP looks like a long-playing record; here it is two initials, L(ife) and P(lanet), both series titles with this world in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Our home planet appears in two series titles: Life on ___ and Planet ___.

definitions.meaning: the phrase 'in ... ' describes something done heartlessly, and a famous feature film carries that title
L is Life: the naturalist's series about reptiles and amphibians was 'Life in ...'

explanation.surface: A cruel element of a programme by the naturalist.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for Life, as in 'Life in Cold Blood', his series on reptiles and amphibians.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in cold blood means doing it callously, without feeling; In Cold Blood is also a film.

clue.text: Get rich female at Tesco's headquarters

parts.note: the head of Tesco is T, and two quarters (compass points) are E and N

explanation.surface: A woman gets wealthy working at the supermarket's head office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headquarters' splits as head (first letter of Tesco) plus quarters, compass points E and N. The entry also reads F ATTEN, the middle of the naturalist's name with his middle initial F.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow fat, plump or rich in a figurative, well-fed sense; 'get rich' as in becoming fleshy or prosperous.

clue.text: Keep secret from William Peter the hermit

parts.note: Peter Noone sang lead in Herman's Hermits

explanation.surface: Hiding something from a solitary named Peter.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter the Hermit was a medieval crusade preacher; here he is Peter Noone, singer of 1960s band Herman's Hermits.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to keep something confidential, sharing it with nobody.

clue.text: Scar possibly could have been rotten

definitions.meaning: Scar plus this word gives the name of a Yorkshire seaside town, so Scar is one example of what can precede it
before 1832 some tiny parliamentary constituencies with almost no voters were called rotten

explanation.surface: A scar that might have gone septic.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarborough is a seaside town in Yorkshire, England. Rotten boroughs were pre-1832 seats with a handful of voters controlled by a patron.
explanation.definitionFit: A town with its own council; Scar- begins one, and a rotten one was a corrupt old constituency.

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are arranged in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A city slicker at a dude ranch falls off and lands badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider thrown from the horse has lost the saddle, as in unseated.

clue.text: Frost maybe when rising doctor is over-keen

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means reading the words upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: An eager doctor gets up in a frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when rising' reverses DR IS to SIRD. Frost is the broadcaster Sir David Frost; the same title and name begin the naturalist's.
explanation.definitionFit: Frost was a knighted broadcaster, so he is one example of a knight with this name.

indicators.note: a problem is something to be worked out, so the letters are to be sorted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Writer's block, the empty page, is a problem for authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's block' is not the creative paralysis but a literal block a writer grinds ink on.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone slab on which solid ink is ground and mixed with water for brush or pen writing.

definitions.meaning: feeling down means sad, low
P is Planet: his ocean series was 'The ... Planet'

explanation.surface: A low moment in the naturalist's planet series.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for Planet; the series is The Blue Planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Sad or depressed is the colour sense; the ocean series is named after it.

indicators.note: a new head means the first letter is swapped for a different one

parts.note: an ogress is a female ogre, a monster

explanation.surface: A monster departing with a replacement head.
explanation.walkthrough: The new head is E, which the clue leaves the solver to find from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The act of going out or departing; also a way out, so a noun for leaving.

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: A river flowing out with a lovely outflow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge' looks like the river's outflow; it means carry out a duty.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a duty is to perform or carry it out, a synonym sense.

clue.text: Opening bid by East in bridge contract

indicators.note: in places the opening of bid and the compass point inside the dental bridge

parts.note: a dental bridge is a kind of denture

indicators.note: this word picks out the opening letter, or opening letters, of the words it governs

explanation.surface: An opening bid made by East in a game of contract bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' takes the first letter of bid; 'bridge' is dental, not the card game the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond or loan agreement issued by a company is a formal financial contract.

definitions.meaning: creatures with wings, flyers
L is Life: his series 'The Life of ...' was about feathered animals

explanation.surface: Football wingers alongside the naturalist's series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wingers' looks like footballers; it means things with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals with feathers and wings are literally wingers; also the subject of The Life of ___.

clue.text: In which L of 18, 14, 16 is problem for chancellor?

definitions.meaning: L is Life: his series about insects and small creatures was 'Life in the ...'
a finance minister worries when the economy expands too slowly

explanation.surface: A programme by the naturalist that also troubles the Chancellor of the Exchequer.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer: too little economic expansion is the Chancellor's problem. The Chancellor of the Exchequer is Britain's finance minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Dense low vegetation is where his insect series was set; split, it is weak economic expansion.

indicators.note: to cast off is to throw away, so the measure is dropped from the sunshade

parts.note: a parasol is a sunshade kind of umbrella
the ell is an old cloth measure

explanation.surface: A sunshade throws a certain amount of shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casts' looks like casting a shadow but signals a removal.
explanation.definitionFit: The darkest part of a shadow, the full shade cast by an eclipse.

clue.text: Man admitted to The Cavern once

indicators.note: letters let into the words that follow sit inside them

explanation.surface: A man let into Liverpool's famous Cavern Club back in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cavern is the Liverpool club where the Beatles played.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name, so 'man' indicates a male first name.

clue.text: What Arctic-bound sailors have for decoration

definitions.meaning: sailors heading for polar seas keep animal pelts down in the hold for warmth
a frill or flounce on a dress

explanation.surface: Sailors heading to the Arctic carry something for ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words: pelts kept beneath deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathered strip or flounce on a skirt or petticoat is ornament; showy trimmings generally.

clue.text: Cloth that spreads pesticide and flies

definitions.meaning: a rag used to wipe furniture clean
a crop-spraying aircraft is known by this name

explanation.surface: A cloth that spreads insect killer and swats flies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flies' looks like the insects the pesticide kills; it is the verb, the plane flying.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaning rag is one sense; a crop-spraying plane is a crop ___, the second sense.

clue.text: Stoop from fever and a hernia

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone stoops because of fever and a hernia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoop' is the noun, an American porch, not bending over.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoop is a porch or raised platform at a house entrance, so a roofed porch.
